entities.summary: Hans Holbein the Elder was a German painter of the early German Renaissance, born in Augsburg, Germany around 1497, and died in 1524. He was the son of Hans Holbein the Younger and brother of Ambrosius Holbein. Holbein the Elder was a court painter to King Henry VIII of England, and his works include the famous portrait of the king, as well as paintings of the Virgin Mary and the Holy Family. His influence can be seen in the works of later artists, such as Lucas Cranach the Elder. Holbein the Elder's paintings are known for their realism and attention to detail, and he was a master of portraiture. He was also a prolific engraver, and his works include intricate designs for books and other printed materials. Through his art, Holbein the Elder helped to shape the visual identity of the English court and the Protestant Reformation in Germany. His legacy can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including the Flemish masters of the 16th century.
